checks: The objective and individual constraint tests are weakly continuous on probabilities on compact S, with the original law itself feasible.

At s<V the finite intersection property yields a finite list of constraints. The image of the probability space is compact and convex, and strict separation from the closed lower orthant forces nonnegative coefficients. The test law μ rules out zero objective coefficient.
After normalization, the point-mass minimum gives the first dual objective. The transformations h=min_S(Q+φ)−φ and φ=−h prove both inequalities for the concave obstacle formulation.

An attaining h saturates both integral inequalities. The nonnegative continuous gap Q−h vanishes on the primal support. Jensen defects in every martingale are nonnegative and have zero integral, hence vanish at each positive source atom.

The affine supporting majorant touches h at the source atom. The conditional mean and Jensen equality give zero integral of its nonnegative gap, whose zero set is closed and convex. Source 0915985a8bcdfd44 §§3–4 assumes attainment only for this part.

dependencies.hypotheses: Each optimizer and μ are compactly supported equal-mass probabilities and satisfy full ambient convex order. Apply the theorem to get a physical martingale. The proof then checks equality for any such martingale, not just an arbitrary conditional kernel.

overlap.comparison: Its compact Strassen result supplies existence of the relevant coupling. It has no quadratic obstacle-value or attaining-contact theorem.

readability: The contact set uses a supporting affine majorant of the concave obstacle. It is separate from the locus where that obstacle touches Q.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The finite-test separation proves equality of both dual suprema, and an attaining obstacle gives the conditional contact characterization.
